stemMd: Suppose Raman finds a boulder whose widest lichen is very nearly the same size as the widest lichens on boulders from a fall recorded 600 years ago. Based on the text, which choice is the most logical conclusion she can draw about this boulder?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed several centuries ago, but its age cannot be narrowed to a particular century.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed more recently than 300 years ago.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The lichen on the boulder began growing before the boulder's face was exposed.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The boulder was exposed roughly 600 years ago, give or take a few years.

explanationMd:
An inference question asks for the strongest claim the text will actually carry — no stronger.

The text gives two facts that bear on this boulder. First, lichen size is a minimum age, and a lichen as wide as those on a 600-year-old fall is a large lichen, so the boulder is old. Second, beyond about 300 years the lichens' growth has slowed so much that Raman's estimates "bunched together, blurring events a century or more apart". Both facts together give exactly Choice D: old, but not datable to a century.

To check an inference, try to state the sentence in the passage that would have to be false for your choice to be wrong. For Choice D nothing has to be false. For Choice A the blurring sentence has to be ignored, and that sentence is the text's whole point about old falls.

distractorRationale.d: This treats a blurred estimate as a precise one. The text says explicitly that past about 300 years the method cannot separate events a century or more apart, so matching a 600-year-old boulder does not pin this one to 600 years.
distractorRationale.c: This contradicts the premise of the method. The passage describes lichens as colonising a face that begins as bare stone, so growth starts after exposure, not before it.
distractorRationale.b: This reverses the reasoning. A very wide lichen indicates a long exposure; it is the small lichens that would indicate a recent fall.

accessibilityText: Using the lichen-dating passage, choose the most logical conclusion about a boulder whose widest lichen nearly matches the widest lichens on boulders from a rockfall recorded 600 years ago.

provenance.notes: Original item. The scenario in the stem is new and is not stated in the passage, so the item tests inference rather than retrieval.

review.author: digital-sat-wave3-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: Past about 300 years the estimates 'bunched together, blurring events a century or more apart', so a lichen matching the 600-year boulders fixes only that the fall is several centuries old, not its century.

review.notes: Author solved and checked uniqueness: the passage supplies both an 'old' signal (wide lichen) and a precision ceiling (blurring past 300 years), and only D respects both. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
